title: Graphs
subtitle: Model relationships as vertices and edges, then choose a frontier or ordering whose invariant matches the question.
variables: V = number of vertices, E = number of input edges (undirected adjacency stores 2E entries), R*C = grid cells, K = number of states per vertex, W = maximum edge weight, Q = queries; S = number of supplied BFS sources. Unless specified, vertices are integer IDs 0..V-1 and adjacency endpoints are valid; inputs are not mutated. Adjacency-list traversal is O(V+E), matrix traversal O(V²). Hash-table costs are expected; long string labels cost O(label length) to hash initially and compare in the worst case, so map to integer IDs for repeated work. Python integers are arbitrary precision: stated arithmetic bounds use a unit-cost bounded-word model. Auxiliary space includes stacks/queues and algorithm state, excludes input and separately identified output. Heap bounds refer to lazy heapq implementations and count duplicate entries. H = heap size; B = allowed edge budget for bounded relaxation. heapq sift work is logarithmic, but CPython list resize can make a single heap operation linear; sequence bounds use amortization. Exact path-count DP may hold exponentially large integers; modulus bounds bit costs.
